title: Motorcycle stage produces 19 arcs vs metriko's 352 on Hand-30k (18x undercount)
description:
Surfaced by PATCH-59 stage 2 motorcycle regression test. Given metriko's known-good stage2 UVs as input + 46 singularities from stage1, our MotorcycleGraph.trace + TMesh.build produce 19 arcs. metriko's stage3_tedges.tsv has 352. We're emitting roughly 1 trace per 2-3 singularities; metriko emits ~7-8.

Hypotheses to check:
1. Each singularity in our impl emits one motorcycle (= one arc) instead of 4 (one per cardinal direction). Metriko emits up to 4 per singularity by default.
2. Our trace terminates early when it loses an injective UV gradient — many singularity wedges may not be injective in the input.
3. Our TMesh.build merges arcs at intersection nodes instead of splitting them — metriko splits each trace into multiple arcs at crash sites.

Per-singularity expected: ~352/46 ≈ 7.6 arcs/singularity. If each singularity has 4 motorcycles each splitting into 2 arcs at intersections, that's 8/singularity. Tracking down exactly which step is dropping arcs is the work.

Diagnostic CLI from PATCH-59: VerifyMetrikoStageDiff (or the regression test) prints arc count diff.
definition-of-done: MotorcycleStageRegressionTest reports our_arc_count within 30% of metriko's 352 on Hand-30k. Existing motorcycle/T-mesh unit tests still pass.
testing-plan: 1. Re-run MetrikoStageRegressionTest.stage2UvsThroughMotorcycleProducesArcs and verify arc count is within bound. 2. Add per-singularity arc count assertion (avg arcs/singularity in [3, 12]).
